fatal_errors: The proposed Ni addition does not match the demonstrated Ta-Nb-V addition.
The claimed FCC solid-solution mediator contradicts the reported HCP-to-BCC phase evolution.
Neither cited source provides evidence that Ni produces an FCC phase or improves ductility and toughness in HfZrTi.
The asserted 10% improvement boundary is arbitrary and unsupported.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general goal of improving HfZrTi ductility and uses the unmodified alloy as a reasonable baseline, but it fails to reconstruct the relevant material intervention or mechanism. The supported intervention is co-addition of Ta, Nb, and V in a 1:1:1 ratio, with sufficiently high additions stabilizing a BCC structure; HfZrTi(TaNbV)0.9 provided the best reported balance, including 16.4% tensile fracture elongation. In contrast, Ni and an FCC mediator are not established by the supplied evidence. The cited papers only discuss general refractory-HEA behavior and typically BCC refractory systems. Tensile testing and microstructural analysis could test the alternative hypothesis, but the design lacks a specified Ni series, processing controls, phase-identification methods, and a valid toughness measurement, while its 10% falsification threshold has no evidentiary basis.
